title: Alice's and Bob's bits are never both set
statement: Consider a coordinate in the disjointness distribution, whose state is one of three cases — belonging to neither player, to Alice only, or to Bob only — and let $\mathrm{xBit}(c)$ and $\mathrm{yBit}(c)$ denote Alice's and Bob's bits in that coordinate. Then for every such coordinate $c$ it is never the case that both $\mathrm{xBit}(c)$ and $\mathrm{yBit}(c)$ equal true.
hypotheses_covered: c ranges over the three-valued disjoint-coordinate type
replaced: A disjoint coordinate-pair never has both bits equal to \texttt{true}.
